lait_frais: Follow the use-by date while sealed. Once opened: 3 days (usual guidance on French cartons). Can be frozen, texture changes.
lait_uht: Sealed: cupboard until the best-before date. Opened: fridge.
lait_vegetal: Sealed UHT carton in the cupboard (best-before date). Opened: 7 to 10 days in the fridge.
lait_coco: Sealed can: cupboard. Opened: move to another container, 7 to 10 days in the fridge.
creme_fraiche: Sealed: use-by date (about 1 month). Opened: 5 to 7 days. Frozen: grainy texture, keep it for cooking.
creme_liquide: Sealed UHT carton in the cupboard. Opened: 5 to 7 days.
beurre: Room temperature 1 to 2 days max (butter dish).
yaourt: Single pot: finish once opened. Large opened pot: 5 to 7 days.
fromage_blanc: Once opened: 3 days (cautious limit, cottage cheese is about 1 week).
mascarpone: About 2 months sealed; we keep the use-by date and 5 days once opened (like opened cream).
mozzarella: Sealed: use-by date. Opened in its brine: 7 to 14 days per StillTasty, 1 to 3 days on French packs: we keep 3 days. Burrata: 1 day.
pate_pressee_cuite: Cut piece: 3 to 4 weeks, well wrapped.
pate_pressee: Tomme and cantal: natural rind, keep in paper.
pate_molle_fleurie: Keeps ripening; raw milk: not advised during pregnancy (ANSES).
chevre_frais: Dry aged goat cheese keeps longer.
feta_saumure: Keep it submerged in the brine.
oeufs: France: best before 28 days after laying, sold unrefrigerated; keep in the fridge at home. Do not freeze in the shell.
preparation_oeufs_crus: ANSES: chill immediately. Cautious 24 h rule (homemade aioli: 3 to 4 days per FoodKeeper).
saucisses_cuites: Sealed: use-by date (USDA 2 weeks). Opened: 7 days.
jambon_blanc: Sealed: use-by date. Opened or sliced at the counter: 3 to 5 days (Listeria).
jambon_cru: Opened tray: 5 days (like opened sliced cured meats).
saucisson_entier: Once cut: keep cool, 2 to 3 weeks.
pate_traiteur: Sliced at the counter: under 3 days per ANSES; FoodKeeper pate 1 to 2 days.
conserve_viande_poisson: Sealed: cupboard (best-before date). Opened: move to another container, 3 to 4 days in the fridge. Bulging can: throw away (ANSES).
coquillages_vivants: Throw away open shells before cooking.
poisson_cuit: Leftovers: 2 days per FSA; FoodKeeper 3 to 4 days; ANSES under 3 days.
saumon_fume: Sealed: use-by date (2 to 3 weeks). Opened: 1 week per StillTasty, 2 to 3 days on French packs; we keep 3 days (Listeria).
tofu: Opened: cover with fresh water, change the water every day.
restes_viande: ANSES under 3 days; FSA 2 days; USDA 3 to 4 days.
plat_sauce: Cool quickly and refrigerate within 2 h (ANSES).
soupe_brique: Opened: 3 to 4 days in the fridge.
quiche: No more than 2 h at room temperature.
riz_cuit: FSA: fridge within 1 h, eat within 24 h (Bacillus cereus); FoodKeeper 4 to 6 days. Freeze within 1 h.
cereales_cuites: FoodKeeper cooked quinoa 6 to 7 days; we apply the ANSES leftovers rule of under 3 days.
salade_composee: Does not freeze well. With mayonnaise: chill immediately.
plat_traiteur: ANSES: deli products and ready meals within 3 days of purchase (if no use-by date).
houmous_maison: FoodKeeper 7 days; ANSES leftovers rule under 3 days.
vinaigrette_maison: With garlic or fresh herbs: shorten.
legumes_huile_maison: Botulism risk if kept at room temperature.
compote_maison: FoodKeeper gives 3 weeks; we keep 7 days for an unsweetened compote.
patisserie_creme: ANSES: cream pastries within 3 days of purchase.
pain_frais: Do not refrigerate (goes stale). Baguette: best the same day.
pate_crue: Sealed roll: use-by date. Homemade crepe batter (egg): 1 day.
fruits_noyau: Ripen at room temperature, then 3 to 5 days in the fridge.
bananes: Ripen at room temperature (3 days once ripe); the skin turns black in the fridge.
melon: Cut: wrap, 2 to 4 days in the fridge.
fruits_exotiques: Pomegranate: 1 to 3 months in the fridge.
avocat: Ripen at room temperature. Cut: lemon and wrap, 3 to 4 days.
fruits_secs: Opened bag: 1 month in the cupboard or 6 months in the fridge.
tomates: USDA advises room temperature (taste); fridge is fine once very ripe.
pommes_de_terre: Cool, dry and dark (cupboard). Freeze only cooked.
ail: Whole head in the cupboard; peeled cloves 3 days in the fridge.
choux: Chinese cabbage / pak choi: 2 to 3 days.
betterave: Vacuum-packed cooked beetroot: use-by date, then 3 days once opened.
asperges: Stand upright in a little water.
courge: Cut: 4 to 5 days in the fridge (like courgette).
herbes_tendres: Bunch in a glass of water or in damp paper.
basilic: Does not like the cold: better at room temperature.
confiture: Opened: 6 to 12 months in the fridge.
compote_commerce: Opened: 7 to 10 days in the fridge.
miel: Honey crystallises without spoiling. Opened maple syrup: fridge.
pate_tartiner: Opened: 2 to 3 months in the cupboard (3 to 4 months in the fridge for natural nut butters).
moutarde: Opened: 12 to 18 months in the fridge (1 to 2 months in the cupboard).
sauce_soja: Opened: 1 month in the fridge (FoodKeeper), for quality.
vinaigrette_commerce: Creamy dressing: 3 to 4 weeks once opened.
sauce_tomate_bocal: Opened: move to another container, 4 days in the fridge.
pesto_bocal: Fresh pesto from the chilled aisle: use-by date. Opened: 3 days (FoodKeeper), cover with oil.
tapenade: Opened: 7 days in the fridge (like shop-bought hummus).
conserve_fruits_legumes: Vegetables (low acid): 3 to 4 days once opened; fruit, tomatoes (acidic): 5 to 7 days.
huile: Opened: 3 to 5 months away from light.
huile_noix: Goes rancid fast: fridge once opened.
farine: Wholemeal or rye flour: 3 months in the cupboard, 6 months in the fridge.
cereales_crues: Quinoa: 2 to 3 years; millet and buckwheat: 2 months (FoodKeeper whole grain).
chocolat: Dry and cool; white bloom is not dangerous.
noix: Go rancid: fridge or freezer for larger stocks. Walnuts: 2 to 4 weeks in the cupboard.
jus_frais: Sealed: use-by date. Opened: 7 to 10 days.
jus_ambiant: Sealed: cupboard. Opened: 7 to 10 days in the fridge.
vin_ouvert: Recork; freeze as ice cubes for cooking.
boisson_lactee: Sealed: use-by date. Opened: 3 days (like fresh milk).
